subject: Offer metadata, billing labels, and usage-example copy for AWS listing
messages:
From: David Lee <david@acmecloud.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marketplace@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft offer + billing labels / usage examples

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the earlier call — attaching our current offer draft and the pricing CSV. AWS asked us to provide two things before certification: clear billing label mappings (how charges surface on customer invoices) and 3 short usage examples that show how a typical customer would consume the SKU. Can you take a quick pass and suggest copy that fits marketplace space limits (title / 1-line / 3 bullets)?

Attached: acme_offer_draft.pdf (proposal), acme_pricing_table.csv

Quick asks:
- One-sentence billing label for the Seller console and what appears on invoices (<= 60 chars)
- One-line usage examples suitable for the product page bullets (each ~120 chars)
- Any red flags for co-sell badging or private offer footnotes

We need to return this to AWS by EOD Monday.

Best,
David
Account Lead, Acme Cloud
---

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Lee <david@acmecloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, marketplace@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft offer + billing labels / usage examples

David — thanks for the materials, looks well organized. Quick pass below (keeping Marketplace char constraints in mind). I copied Marissa since she'll flag any co-sell optics.

Billing label (short): Redwood x Acme - Inference Units
Rationale: keeps vendor identity, references "Inference" to map to usage-based line items. <= 40 chars.

Product page one-line (hero): High-throughput LLM inference for secure customer-facing apps — predictable latency and cost.
(~~110 chars)

Three usage-example bullets (short):
- Real-time chat: scale to 30k messages/day with 99th% latency < 300ms per request.
- Batch embeddings: generate semantic indexes for 10M docs in parallel with spot-compatible workers.
- Private deployments: run inference inside your VPC with audit logs and KMS integrations.

Pricing footnote suggestion for private offers: "Private offers may include committed monthly capacity and custom pricing; invoice line items will list 'Redwood x Acme - Inference Units' and usage breakdown by model."

Red flags: avoid phrasing that implies we host customer data outside region (they're EU customers sometimes). Also, be careful with "unlimited throughput" claims.

Attachment: suggested copy file attached (I exported as small text snippet for AWS).

If that looks right I'll prepare a trimmed version for the marketplace fields (title/short/3 bullets) and hand to Marissa for co-sell badge checks.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Programs
Redwood Inference
---

All — quick notes from a co-sell / GTM lens: 

1) Badging: we can request "Co-sell eligible" badge if Acme is on our partner list and we provide a one-pager with customer success stories. Marissa action: I'll draft the 1-pager template and send by Monday.

2) Visibility: For AWS private offers, include a short "How to contact Redwood" blurb (1 line) so the buyer knows who to loop in for infra/SLAs. Suggestion: "Contact Redwood Inference for enterprise onboarding and SLA details."

3) Usage bullets: tweak the first two to be less prescriptive about exact #s — marketplace reviewers sometimes push back on hard SLA numbers without public metrics. Suggest: "Real-time chat: low-latency inference for high-throughput conversational applications."

4) Billing label: Kim's label is fine. Ben — please confirm there's no internal pricing SKU naming conflict.

I'll take the trimmed marketplace-length copy from Kimberly and produce a co-sell ready bundle (1-pager + case study stub).

—Marissa
Sr. Partner GTM Manager, Redwood Inference
